events.claim: Parliamentary proceedings for both the House and Senate were published for 7 September 2026.
Roy Morgan measured Labor primary vote at 27.0% in fieldwork conducted 31 August to 6 September 2026.
Roy Morgan measured One Nation primary vote at 26.5% in fieldwork conducted 31 August to 6 September 2026.
Roy Morgan measured Liberal primary vote at 17.0% in fieldwork conducted 31 August to 6 September 2026.
Roy Morgan measured Greens primary vote at 14.5% in fieldwork conducted 31 August to 6 September 2026.
Roy Morgan measured Nationals primary vote at 4.5% in fieldwork conducted 31 August to 6 September 2026.
The Australian Greens announced Vanessa Bleyer had joined the federal team and taken Agriculture, Science/Industry/Innovation, Tourism and Healthy Oceans portfolios.
The Australian Greens announced David Shoebridge as spokesperson for Digital Rights and AI.
The Liberal Party published a Coalition illicit-tobacco policy proposing an 80% tobacco excise cut, regulated adult nicotine products and a $200 million enforcement surge.
One Nation published a tobacco policy proposing a 75% tobacco excise cut, a three-year indexation pause and tougher enforcement against illicit tobacco.
Labor published that the 100th residential housing development had received EPBC Act approval and attributed more than 80,000 approved homes to the government's national environmental-law approvals.
Parliament of Australia listed both federal chambers as sitting on 8 September 2026, with the House and Senate scheduled from 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM AEST.

The Liberal Party published a same-day release using NSW Premier Chris Minns' tobacco-tax comments to frame a policy split within Labor. This records an observed opposition messaging signal; the framing remains attributed to the Liberal Party.
NSW Government opened public exhibition of a draft Woollahra and Edgecliff rezoning proposal on 8 September 2026 and stated that the proposal could support up to 9,400 homes.

One Nation Victoria listed an 8 September Blackburn campaign event featuring Jamie Baker for Box Hill and Natalie Adams for North-Eastern Metro. This records observable candidate campaign activity, not an inference about electoral effect.
